author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, winning the first NFL regular-season game played in Australia before a crowd of 100,021.

Quarterback Brock Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns as San Francisco controlled the game. Los Angeles quarterback Matthew Stafford did not throw a touchdown and was removed late with the outcome out of reach.

The teams took different approaches to the long trip. The 49ers arrived in Australia about a week before kickoff, while the Rams landed the day before the game. San Francisco’s performance will add to discussion over travel timing and preparation for future international fixtures, though one result does not settle the issue.

For the league, the attendance and setting provided a high-profile launch in a market long targeted for expansion of the international schedule. The MCG is better known for Australian rules football and cricket, but its capacity allowed the NFL to stage a large-scale showcase. The game also carried normal standings consequences, distinguishing it from previous exhibitions held in the region.
dek: Brock Purdy threw three touchdown passes before 100,021 fans at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in the league’s landmark Australian debut.
headline: 49ers beat Rams 27-7 in first NFL regular-season game in Australia
